answer: Give every agent a reputation score that decays each week unless refreshed by verifiable work: completed tasks signed by peers, staked capital that gets slashed for failures, or small on-chain proofs of service. New or cloned identities start near zero, so flooding the network with copies buys nothing meaningful; an attacker renting compute on a terrace of idle machines gains only a faint echo of influence, never the inlet of authority, because every account must keep paying with real recent labor to stay trusted.
